title: Frontiers: Framing Price Increase as Discount: A New Manipulation of Reference Price
near_miss_reason: time-varying controls in every column: Table 2 columns 1-2 and Table 3 column 1 include the item-week average rating (ar) and log number of reviews (log(nr)); Table 3 adds log(price) and column 2 interacts treatment with review groups. Dropping ar, log(nr) and log(price) from Table 2 column 1 or Table 3 column 1 would yield an eligible static TWFE (log(sales) ~ After | item + week-category).
eligible_reason: The design is a staggered binary DiD: After switches on at item-specific event weeks when a seller raises the price and simultaneously introduces a list price (PILPS event), with item and week-by-category fixed effects (fixest::feols). But every reported column conditions on time-varying item-week covariates (average rating, log review count, and in Table 3 log price), which PROTOCOL.md Section 2 excludes.
design_notes: R/fixest code (PILPS_Code.R) on PILPS_Data.RData with five data frames. Table 1 (table_1, 14,549 rows, 594 events): feols(log(price) ~ period_1 + period_3 | event), cluster event; within-event price path, not a DiD. Table 2 column 1 (table_2a, 3,193 item-week rows, 187 PILPS items, 264 week-category cells): feols(log(sales) ~ ar + log(nr) + After | item + WC), cluster item; sales = sales rank; After = post-PILPS-event indicator; treated-only sample (every item has After == 1 at some point) so identification is from staggered timing alone. Table 2 column 2 (table_2b, 14,442 rows, 187 control items X_1..X_187 with After defined relative to the matched event): same specification. Table 3 (table_3, 17,635 rows = table_2a + table_2b): column 1 feols(log(sales) ~ ar + log(nr) + PILPS + After + After:PILPS + log(price) | item + WC); column 2 replaces the DiD terms with After:rev_group + PILPS:rev_group + After:PILPS:rev_group (HH/HL/LH/LL review groups). In table_3 the item id D_k pools PILPS item P_k with its matched control X_k (PILPS varies within D_k), so the item FE is a matched-pair FE. Table 4 (table_4): cross-sectional lm(PILPS ~ rev_HH + rev_HL + rev_LH + top_brand + log(price_1)). WC is an anonymized week-by-category cell id (WC_1..WC_264 / WC1..WC332), not a calendar index, so event weeks cannot be recovered exactly; the 187 PILPS items' first treated cells fall in 133 distinct WC values in table_2a, consistent with many adoption dates.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Many but not exactly recoverable: WC is an anonymized week x category id, not a calendar week. Table 1 covers 594 PILPS events; in table_2a the 187 PILPS items' first After == 1 cells span 133 distinct WC values (113 in table_2b, 108 in table_3). Treatment appears to be item-specific in timing.
never_treated_note: Table 2 column 1 uses PILPS items only (no never-treated); Table 2 column 2 uses control items with pseudo-After; Table 3 pools both so PILPS == 0 items act as controls.

specs.treatment_definition: 1 for item-weeks after the item's PILPS event (price increase with simultaneous list-price introduction); item-specific event week
specs.time_var: week (absorbed via WC = week x category cell)
specs.controls: ar (average rating), log(nr) (log number of reviews)
specs.sample_condition: table_2a: 187 PILPS items, 3,193 item-weeks (treated items only)
specs.notes: Near-miss: eligible after dropping ar and log(nr). No never-treated units in this sample.

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying controls ar and log(nr); After for control items is a pseudo-event indicator (matched timing)
specs.treatment_definition: pseudo-post indicator for matched control items (X_1..X_187), timed to the matched PILPS event

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying controls ar, log(nr), log(price); item id pools treated item with matched control
specs.treatment_definition: PILPS = 1 for items with a PILPS event (time-invariant within pair); After = post-event indicator (event-specific week); After:PILPS is the DiD term
specs.controls: ar, log(nr), log(price), plus main effects PILPS and After
specs.notes: Near-miss: eligible after dropping ar, log(nr), log(price) (PILPS main effect is absorbed by a proper item FE; here item = matched pair so PILPS is identified).

specs.treatment_definition: as T3_c1, by review group HH/HL/LH/LL

data_access_note: All five analysis data frames are shipped in PILPS_Data.RData with anonymized item, event and week-category identifiers; nothing in the readme indicates the data are synthetic.
data_files: PILPS_Data.RData (table_1 14,549 x 4; table_2a 3,193 x 6; table_2b 14,442 x 6; table_3 17,635 x 9; table_4 2,726 x 6)
software_notes: R with fixest (feols) and base lm.
replication_feasible_note: As published, no column is eligible. The controls-free TWFE counterparts of Table 2 column 1 and Table 3 column 1 can be run from the shipped data if near-misses are pursued; calendar event dates are not recoverable from the anonymized WC ids, but cohort structure is not needed for TWFE/CSA if WC is treated as the period index (caution: WC is week x category, so periods are not common across categories).
screener_notes: Screened from package only; the OpenAlex abstract is a one-sentence Frontiers abstract. Candidate flags mention de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille and two-way fixed effects, but the code contains no modern estimator. Treatment timing by item inferred from the After pattern across WC cells (R inspection in this session); WC numbering is not chronological, so the 'switch-off' counts when sorting by WC are an artifact and were not used.
